title: Spot the Spin
description: Read the following news excerpt and identify the bias techniques being used. Each question tests a different critical thinking skill.
article: The radical new tax proposal, championed by out-of-touch politicians, would devastate hardworking families while lining the pockets of government bureaucrats. Some economists — mostly those with ties to left-wing think tanks — claim it could reduce inequality, but real experts warn of catastrophic consequences for job creators.

questions.text: Which phrase in the excerpt uses loaded language to frame politicians negatively?
questions.explanation: 'Out-of-touch' is a loaded phrase that implies politicians are disconnected from ordinary people, framing them negatively without evidence.

questions.text: What bias technique is used when the article says 'mostly those with ties to left-wing think tanks'?
questions.explanation: This discredits the economists by implying political bias rather than engaging with their actual arguments — a classic ad hominem technique.

questions.text: The phrase 'real experts warn of catastrophic consequences' is an example of:
questions.explanation: 'Real experts' implies other experts are fake, while 'catastrophic' is emotionally loaded. No specific experts or evidence are cited.

questions.text: Which perspective is completely absent from this excerpt?
questions.explanation: While the article claims to speak for 'hardworking families,' it never actually quotes or represents people who might benefit from reduced inequality.
